_comment: Bundle size budgets, in kilobytes of gzipped JavaScript.
The shared budget is the one that matters most. Every route pays it, so a
library that leaks into the shared chunk is charged to the gate scanner —
the screen that runs on cheap tablets over poor connections and must stay
fast. Framer Motion, Three.js and Sonner are deliberately per-page or
dynamically imported; if `shared` climbs, one of them has escaped.
Headroom is deliberately thin (~2%). Any real library is more than 5 kB
gzipped, so a leak trips this immediately, while a React or Next patch
Raise a budget only with a reason recorded in docs/OUTPUT_LOGS.md.
